title: An exact middle term inherits a mixed upper weight bound
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $S_0$ put $S=S_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use the common-stage coefficient category $D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$ and its constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Weil objects and equivariant morphisms are fixed pairs as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Mixed upper bounds and $D_{\le w}(S_0)$ have the meanings of [def-weil-punctual-weights; def-weil-complex-weights].

Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, let $u\in\mathbf R$, and let
$$A\xrightarrow{a}B\xrightarrow{b}C$$
be morphisms of constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $Y_0$, exact at $B$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. If $A$ and $C$ are $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $u$, then $B$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $u$. Neither injectivity of $a$ nor surjectivity of $b$ is assumed.

source.place: Step 0: exact sequences of sheaves; old step 1.

proof.text: Work in the abelian category of constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves specified in [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand], with the common-stage heart of the statement. Put $B'=\operatorname{im}(a)\subset B$ and $Q=B/B'$. Exactness at $B$ means $B'=\ker(b)$ by [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Thus $A\twoheadrightarrow B'$ is a Weil quotient and $b$ induces a Weil map $\bar b:Q\to C$ with kernel $\ker(b)/B'=0$, so $Q$ is a Weil subobject of $C$. The quotient projection has kernel $B'$, giving $0\to B'\to B\to Q\to0$. These are the elementary image and quotient constructions in the stated abelian category; in particular all the objects remain constructible and all arrows retain their Weil structures.

source.place: Step 0: exact sequences of sheaves; old step 1.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] first to the Weil quotient $A\twoheadrightarrow B'$ and then to the Weil subobject $Q\hookrightarrow C$. The hypotheses on $A$ and $C$ give that both $B'$ and $Q$ are $\iota$-mixed of weights at most the same real number $u$. Neither of these applications requires $a$ to be injective or $b$ to be surjective.

source.place: Step 0: exact sequences of sheaves; old step 1.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] to the short exact sequence $0\to B'\to B\to Q\to0$ from step 1. Step 2 supplies both outer mixed upper bounds with $w=u$, and the extension clause gives that $B$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $u$, as required.
